question: phase 3 found the Dirac rotation of the valley-0 1s at 0.85-0.87 Za c sin(theta) at a = 0.5: does the missing ~13 % go down with a, and with what law?

setup.box: 24 lambda_C (same as the Laboratorio at a = 0.5), Z = 60, nucleus on the corner of 8 cells
setup.nucleus: NUCLEO_1S sec. 14 transferred nucleus: s(a) = s(0.5) + (s(0.3) - s(0.5)) (a - 0.5)/(0.3 - 0.5), s(0.5) = (0.554593, 1.003549), s(0.3) = (0.57482, 1.002538), factors on the 8 cells at r0 = sqrt3/2 a and the 24 cells at r1 = sqrt11/2 a. a = 0.4 and 0.25 were never used to learn.
setup.preparation: as phase 3, rescaled to the same physical times: seed = radial Dirac 1s (spin up); pass 0: autocorrelation spectrum over 1024/a ticks (= 2048 at a = 0.5), Hann, peak in 0.86..0.94; passes 1 and 2: filtering at the peak (1024/a ticks each, pass 2 from the pass-1 state); projection on valley k = 0 (same Fourier cells as phase 2/3), normalised. Change from phase 3, declared: pass 1 of phase 3 accumulated 33 candidate frequencies at once; here the peak comes from the spectrum alone (memory at 96^3), then 2 filtering passes.
setup.run: physical time 2000 lambda_C/c (4000 ticks at a = 0.5, 8000 at a = 0.25), 2e5 exact surfers (two-tick flow), Born start; 5 surfer windows of ~5 lambda_C/c (10 a/c at a = 0.5) starting at t = 250, 500, 1000, 1500 lambda_C/c and one closing at the end of the run (the 3990 window of phase 3, now measured); records every 50 lambda_C/c.
setup.v_of_a: v(a) = mean of the surfer v_phi/(Za sin) of the two early windows (250, 500), before the slow valley beat; deficit d(a) = 1 - v(a)

G1.what: every a: prepared state valley-0 weight >= 0.99 and <Sigma_z> >= 0.9

G2.what: every a: fidelity >= 0.9 and valley-0 weight >= 0.9 at every record and at the end

G3.what: every a: surfer v_phi/(Za sin) in [0.75, 1.25] in all 5 windows (including the end window)

G5.what: the deficit goes down with a: d(0.5) > d(0.4) > d(0.3) > d(0.25)

G6.what: continuum limit: least-squares d(a) = d0 + c1 a on the 4 lattices, |d0| <= 0.05 (Dirac recovered within 5 %); also reported: d = C a^p (p, R^2) and d0 + c2 a^2
